title: parallel-model-switchbench-notes-marion
content:
Objective:
Quick experiments to quantify latency and throughput impact when the routing layer switches requests between model variants mid-session or routes different concurrent requests to different model families on the same GPU ("mesh-batching"). Goal is to identify dominant overheads and suggest mitigations for SLOs (p95/p99 <= target).

Background / motivation:
- Recent customer cases want per-request model selection (cheap->expensive) depending on prompt safety/quality heuristics. We route in-traffic: some requests start on lightweight 7B and may be escalated to 13B mid-generation if score threshold triggers.
- Hypothesis: switching mid-KV cache (context / prefix) or switching the active GPU kernel set has non-trivial per-token latency penalty and can degrade p99 under bursty arrival.
- Also exploring mesh-batching: co-locating multiple models on one GPU and attempting to batch across them (same device, different kernel paths) to improve utilization.

Setup:
- Hardware: 1x A100-40GB instance per run (dev farm slice), CUDA 12.2, cuBLAS/cuDNN latest in image.
- Runtime: local dev build of serving runtime (branch: feature/mesh-switchbench PR 4321).
- Models tested: redwood-small-7b-q4 (quantized), llama-2-13b-ggml (float16), gpt-neox-20b-micro (sharded reduced context for smoke).
- Batching behavior: continuous-batching enabled (max-batch=64, batch-timeout-ms=6), dynamic KV cache allocation.
- Workloads: synthetic arrival generator (zipfian) producing 50–1000 qps; per-request sequence lengths: seed 40 tokens + generated 160 tokens target; escalation chance: configurable (0%, 10%, 30%).
- Measurements: p50/p95/p99 token latency (ms), end-to-end latency (ms), observed QPS, GPU utilization, context switch time measured via custom span around model swap code path.

Experiment matrix (representative runs):
- A: baseline single-model 7B (no switching), 200 qps steady, 10k requests.
- B: mid-request escalation 7B->13B with KV transfer (copy prefix to new model), 200 qps, escalation=10%.
- C: mid-request escalation 7B->13B with fast-stubbed fallback (recompute from scratch on 13B without transfer), 200 qps, escalation=10%.
- D: mesh-batching co-locating 7B + 13B on same GPU, routing mixed 200 qps, static ratio 70/30, try cross-model batching enabled.
- E: stress runs at 800 qps with same mixes to observe tail effects.

Raw results (selected aggregates) -- median of 3 runs where applicable:
- Run A (7B only): p50 token=6.8ms, p95 token=17.3ms, p99 token=28.9ms, end2end avg=420ms, GPU util=61%.
- Run B (KV transfer): p50 token=8.5ms, p95 token=26.8ms, p99 token=64.2ms, end2end avg=760ms, GPU util=63%, measured model-swap span avg=18ms (KV serialization+transfer+kernel rebind).
- Run C (recompute on 13B): p50 token=10.9ms, p95 token=34.5ms, p99 token=89.1ms, end2end avg=980ms, GPU util=71%, model-swap span avg=48ms (extra compute + blocking).
- Run D (mesh-batch cross-model): p50 token=7.6ms, p95 token=22.1ms, p99 token=55.4ms, end2end avg=690ms, GPU util=78%, observed small increases in kernel-launch count and occasional kernel contention. Cross-batch merge success rate ~43% (i.e., fraction of batches where tokens from both models were coalesced rather than serialized).
- Run E (800 qps mixed): p50 token=9.8ms, p95 token=44.2ms, p99 token=210ms, end2end avg=1.3s, GPU util=92%, saturation-induced queueing visible (token p99 spikes align with short windows of kernel contention).

Observations / notes:
1) KV transfer path is cheaper than full recompute in p50/p95, but can still produce large p99 spikes when it collides with batch boundary/coalescing logic. The 18ms avg swap span does not capture worst-case serialization mutex waits (observed up to 120ms in some traces).
2) Recompute fallback (run C) guarantees correctness but amplifies p99 significantly due to blocking additional compute on shared device. Not acceptable for strict p99 SLOs unless we cap concurrency during escalations.
3) Mesh-batching shows promise: improves util and reduces average end2end vs naive serializing but only when cross-batch merge rate is moderate (>40%). High variance arrival reduces merge opportunities and increases kernel churn.
4) At high QPS (Run E), tail dominates from two sources: (a) queueing behind long regeneration on 13B (b) transient kernel launch throttling when many different kernel configs are toggled quickly.
5) Measured kernel rebind/selector cost ~6–12ms on this runtime image (hot path), and KV serialization (copying from 7B cache format to 13B format) ~6–30ms depending on prefix length. These are actionable targets.

Quick conclusions / recommendations:
- Do NOT enable full mid-request recompute escalation by default; prefer KV transfer path with conservative gating.
- Implement an "escalation budget" token counter per GPU: throttle escalations if >X concurrent escalations to keep p99 bounded.
- Add an adaptive merge window for mesh-batching: increase batch-timeout slightly (e.g., +2ms) when cross-model-ratio is high to improve merge rate, but make it adaptive to latency windows.
- Optimize KV serialization: switch to zero-copy shared format between 7B and 13B variants (prototype idea) to remove the 6–30ms copy.
- Cache kernel selector results for recent model-pairs to avoid repeated rebind cost.

Traces / artifacts attached / TODOs:
- TODO: add flamegraphs for Run B p99 spike (Ibrahim to collect).
- TODO: reproduce worst-case 120ms lock contention and root-cause in scheduler (Sana).
- TODO: implement simple escalation budget proof-of-concept on dev branch and run a 1k qps smoke.
- Notebook: quick viz script (not checked in) at /notebooks/mesh-switchbench/plot_runs.ipynb (local).

Quick reproducible command snippet (dev farm):
./tools/run_synth_load --qps 200 --model 7b --escalation-mode transfer --escalation-prob 0.1 --seed 42 --duration 600s 

Notes-to-self / heuristics learned:
- Keep escalation probability small in prod gating (<5%) until we have escalation budgets enforced.
- Avoid even small kernel rebinds during known burst windows (deploy window scheduling).
- Mesh-batching needs better telemetry (per-batch composition) to make adaptive windowing safe.

If time: run the same matrix on a 2x A100 (multi-GPU pin) to see if cross-device migration costs behave differently and whether we can route escalations to a different GPU instead of same-device switch.

End of scratchpad.
